messages:
alejandra: Quick follow-up on the active/active RFC — we need to decide how proxy hints interact with hard residency constraints for EU tenants. TL;DR: current fallback order can route EU-resident writes to US when EU capacity is low, which could be a compliance problem for PII. Do we: deny, escrow, or allow+audit?

mike: Do we have a tenant-level flag already? I thought control-plane has tenant.residency = EU. We could enforce a hard deny in the proxy if tenant is EU and target region != eu-west.

samir: Hard deny is safest legally but awful for availability. Another option: an escrow/quarantine pattern — accept the write only if we can land it in an EU-scoped escrow store and mark it as 'pending-mirrored'. Async mirror to global primary once EU consents/recovers. Read semantics get tricky.

lucy: Ops concerns: escrow adds stateful queues and TTLs, operator runbooks, and SLO fallout (clients see higher latencies). Alternative is to return 503 with an error code clients can surface. Simpler but requires client work.

alejandra: Thinking in terms of explicit modes we can expose:
  - strict: proxy denies cross-region writes (compliance-first)
  - escrow: accept into EU escrow, surface audit id, async mirror, show in console
  - soft: route as today, but tag, log, alert on cross-region writes
We need an API/control-plane contract and console telemetry for each.

mike: Proposal: add header X-Residence-Policy: strict|escrow|soft that overrides tenant default. Tenant default set in control plane (tenant.metadata.residency_policy). Metrics: residency.fallback_count, residency.escrow_queue_length.

samir: For escrow impl sketch: reuse existing prewrite queue service but scoped to region and tenant. Add cryptographic audit log entry on enqueue (hash + signature) so we can prove residency was respected. Also add a small read-path: if a key is in escrow, reads return a 'pending' status with last-writable-version.

infra-bot: deploy-notification: canary flag region_hint_policy=v2 scheduled for 2026-04-02 (10% rollout).

lucy: Ops runbook ask: when fallback_rate > 1% over 5m for a region, trigger pre-warm of EU prefetch pools and page on-call. Also define storage thresholds for escrow to avoid overload.

alejandra: Action items: (1) add X-Residence-Policy header + tenant default in control plane (mike) (2) design escrow API + audit log + read semantics (samir) (3) telemetry + alerts + console widgets (lucy) (4) runbook prewarm threshold and operator playbook (lucy). I will write RFC follow-up doc with these modes and examples.

mike: I'll take (1), will sketch API today and open PR for proxy enforcement.

samir: I'll do (2). pairing with mike on the enqueue interface sounds good — lunch pairing?

lucy: I'll draft the runbook pages and alert rules. Will add dashboard panels for escrow queue and fallback ratio.

alejandra: Great — tagging for visibility: @mike @samir @lucy. We'll convert the notes into an RFC addendum this week. :thumbsup:
